node.title: Re^2: A little golfing challenge: replace digits by random letters (updated) -- oneliner
node.author: Eily
node.doctext:
or.. (shorter than Eily's one ;)

perl -pe 's|\d|(a..z)[$&-time%7]|eg' input.txt
That's nearly always correct (if you ignore the fact that it's a shift, not a shuffle). You'll get different values if the lines are not treated in the same second. This would happen if the first line is handled at 9:59:59.9999 and the second at 10:00:00.0000 (add the proper number of digits). Or if you are working on a piped input from a slow program, or the input is big enough. This can be demonstrated by [https://webperl.zero-g.net/democode/perleditor.html#%7B%22cmdline%22%3A%22perl%20-pe%20's%7C%5C%5Cd%7C(a..z)%5B%24%26-time%257%5D%7Ceg%3B%20sleep%201'%20input.txt%22%2C%22inputs%22%3A%5B%7B%22fn%22%3A%22input.txt%22%2C%22text%22%3A%22%3C0123456789%3E%5Cn%3C0123456789%3E%5Cn000%5Cn111%5Cn222%22%7D%5D%2C%22autorun%22%3Atrue%7D|adding a sleep].

I realized I could [https://webperl.zero-g.net/democode/perleditor.html#%7B%22cmdline%22%3A%22perl%20-pe%20'%40h%7Ba..z%7D%3D1%3Bs%2F%5C%5Cd%2F(%25h)%5B%24%26*2%5D%2Feg'%20input.txt%22%2C%22inputs%22%3A%5B%7B%22fn%22%3A%22input.txt%22%2C%22text%22%3A%22%3C0123456789%3E%5Cn%3C0123456789%3E%22%7D%5D%2C%22autorun%22%3Atrue%7D|shorten the other version] (I don't feel like calling it mine when I just took your idea and rewrote it :P), but it's still longer than your latest proposition: perl -pe '@h{a..z}=1;s/\d/(%h)[$&*2]/eg' input.txt

Because since this is golfing, why would you bother doing things properly/efficiently? :P
